# Epic: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

## Problem

The shipped attract/demo bot (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ and its follow-ups) is a
per-frame priority ladder with a reaction-time governor bolted on. It has no
commitment, no forward model, no aim/fire reasoning and no way to learn from
human play, so it reads as random and cannot be tuned into competence. We need
a **maintainable bot framework** that plays competently and human-like, adapts
to new content (enemies, power-ups, weapons) without a rewrite, can be re-run
headless for reproducible evaluation, and is backed by **telemetry** gathered
both from our own recordings and from production playtesters.

## Goals / user stories

- **As the maintainer**, I can re-run the bot headless on a fixed seed and get
  reproducible results, so I can improve it safely.
- **As the maintainer**, I can add a new enemy / power-up / weapon and have the
  bot handle it through configuration, without touching the core.
- **As the maintainer**, I can record human play and analyse it (reaction
  times, target choices, engagement distances, dodge behaviour) to tune and
  evaluate the bot.
- **As the maintainer**, I can enable opt-in telemetry in production and gather
  playtester data (state + input + events) to improve the bot and the game.
- **As a player**, I see an attract/demo mode that looks like a competent
  player.

## Design overview

- **Determinism.** A per-run **seed** drives all gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/
  timing) so a run is reproducible and the bot can be evaluated same-seed.
- **Telemetry.** A **versioned, consent-gated, pluggable** pipeline. Records
  are per-tick state + input + discrete events, tagged with the run seed and a
  schema version. Sinks: a local JSONL dev sink and a production remote sink.
  No PII; **disabled by default in production**, opt-in only.
- **Bot framework.** A world model (from `BotSnapshot`), a **registry of
  goals/behaviours**, a **utility selector with commitment/hysteresis**, a
  behaviour-tree executor, and predictive **dodge/aim** behaviours.
  Content-specific parameters live in a **config/registry** so new content is
  data, not code.
- **Evaluation.** Same-seed bot-vs-human runs, metrics, A/B comparisons and
  side-by-side clips.
- **Style matching (later).** Fit parameters or train a policy from recorded
  telemetry once the competent bot exists.

## Epic acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Runs are reproducible from a seed; the seed is recorded in
  telemetry; a headless runner executes the bot for N ticks on a seed and
  produces a deterministic report.
- **AC2:** Telemetry is a pluggable framework with a documented, versioned
  schema, disabled by default in production and opt-in consent-gated; it
  records per-tick state + input + events with the seed and is a no-op when
  disabled.
- **AC3:** The bot is a structured framework (world model + goal/behaviour
  registry + committed selection + predictive dodge/aim), not a per-frame
  priority ladder; new enemies/power-ups/weapons are handled via config with
  tests.
- **AC4:** The competent bot completes representative runs with human-like
  behaviour (goal commitment, no suicide, human cadence) and passes an
  evaluation report (survival, minerals/min, targets engaged, dodges).
- **AC5:** Human play can be recorded and analysed offline, and a replay/ghost
  viewer compares bot vs human on the same seed.
- **AC6:** Production telemetry can be enabled by a playtester via an explicit
  opt-in, with privacy documentation and no PII.
- **AC7:** All documentation is updated (framework, extension guide, telemetry
  schema/privacy); full suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- A fully style-matched clone of a specific player (style matching is an
  early-phase deliverable; full fidelity is a later follow-up).
- Server-side ML training infrastructure or online multiplayer.
- CI wiring of the capture/eval jobs (follow-up once the harness exists).

## Children (dependency order)

1. Deterministic run seeding + seed plumbing.
2. Telemetry framework (versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag).
3. Game telemetry instrumentation (per-tick state + events).
4. Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling.
5. Bot framework core (world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy,
   content config).
6. Structured competent bot (utility goals + behaviour tree + predictive
   dodge/aim).
7. Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons.
8. Same-seed evaluation harness (metrics, A/B, side-by-side clips).
9. Style matching from telemetry (parameter fitting / imitation).
10. Production telemetry (opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink, docs).

## Related work

Builds on AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ (Smart capture bot) and its follow-ups
AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB (human-like input) and AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L (movement
goals). Supersedes the per-frame priority-ladder design.
data.title: Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry

data.description:
Discovered while implementing AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO (discovered-from:AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO).

## Problem
`npm run build` fails inside any `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` worktree because `scripts/build-audio.mjs` cannot find the sibling ToneForge CLI, so the copied `node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js` tries to `import 'tsx'` and Node cannot resolve it (ToneForge's `tsx` devDependency is only installed in the sibling `../ToneForge/node_modules`).

Error:
```
Error: tf generate failed for aihell-arc-fire seed 32217:
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from .../node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause
`resolveToneForge()` in `scripts/build-audio.mjs` looks for the sibling at `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge', 'bin', 'dev-cli.js')`. In a worktree, `repoRoot` is the worktree directory (nested under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/`), so `repoRoot/..` is not the main checkout's parent. It falls through to `command -v tf`, which finds the worktree's symlinked `node_modules/.bin/tf` (the copy without resolvable `tsx`). In the main checkout the sibling is found and the build passes.

## Impact
Blocks `implement.py finish` (build gate) for **every** epic child (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) and any future worktree-based implementation that runs `npm run build`.

## Workaround (unblocks now, no code change)
```sh
TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build
```
`resolveToneForge()` honours `TONEFORGE_CLI`, and the sibling CLI resolves its own `tsx`.

## Suggested fix
When `repoRoot/../ToneForge` is absent, resolve the main checkout from git (e.g. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` -> parent) and probe `<main>/../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` before falling back to `command -v tf`. Add a hermetic test for worktree-style `repoRoot` resolution.


## Local mitigation only — not a durable fix

As of 2026-10-08 a **local, gitignored** symlink supplies the sibling that the naive probe looks for:

```
.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge -> /home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge
```

This makes `repoRoot/../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` resolve for any worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/`, so worktree builds (and the `implement.py finish` build gate) now pass **on this machine**. It was created during the session for Create full video playthroughs (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) as a deliberate local unblock.

It is **not** part of the repository (`.worklog/` is gitignored) and no script or hook creates it, so the defect remains on a fresh clone, another machine, CI, or if `.worklog/worktrees/` is recreated. The source-level fix and hermetic test proposed above are still outstanding — keep this item open until the durable fix lands.


## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling `../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` next to the **main checkout** when called from a `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` worktree, before falling back to `command -v tf`.
- AC2: Resolution prefers, in order: `TONEFORGE_CLI` env, sibling next to `repoRoot`, sibling next to the main checkout, `tf`/`toneforge` on PATH; returns null when none exist.
- AC3: `npm run build` (build-audio) succeeds inside a worktree without setting `TONEFORGE_CLI`.
- AC4: Hermetic unit tests cover: worktree→main-checkout sibling resolution, `TONEFORGE_CLI` precedence, and the null case.
- AC5: Type declarations (`scripts/build-audio.d.mts`) and existing tests remain correct; full suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Worktree builds fail: build-audio cannot resolve the sibling ToneForge CLI

# Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss to require 200 hits total (readable as 4 phases of 50) and I want its health bar pinned to the top of the screen so I can always read my progress regardless of where the boss is.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC1 and AC4.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` and `_totalHp = BOSS_PHASE_COUNT * BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` (400 total). Doc comment and `BossConfig.initialHp` comment reference 400/100.
- `healthBarGraphics` is created with `scene.add.graphics()`, then `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` puts it in the boss **container**, so it renders offset by the boss position even though `_drawHealthBar()` uses screen coordinates and `setScrollFactor(0)`.
- `getHpFraction()` is already proportional and the four phase-segment dividers already exist — keep both.

## Desired change

1. Change `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE` to `50`; total becomes **200**. Update every comment/constant reference from 100/400 to 50/200 (including `BossConfig.initialHp` docs).
2. Remove the `this.add(this.healthBarGraphics)` container membership so the bar is a **scene child** (it is already created via `scene.add.graphics()`); keep `setScrollFactor(0)` and `setDepth(100)`. It now renders at the absolute screen coordinates drawn by `_drawHealthBar()` (horizontally centred at `BOSS_HEALTH_BAR_Y`).
3. Keep the proportional fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
4. Ensure `destroy()` still explicitly destroys `healthBarGraphics`.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — HP constants/comments, health-bar re-parenting.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — health-model and health-bar placement tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym health-bar placement expectations.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — health-bar layering assumptions if any.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE === 50` and total HP is 200; hitting 49 times keeps phase 1, the 50th hit advances to phase 2, and the 200th hit destroys the boss.
- The health bar Graphics is **not** a child of the boss container and its screen position is unchanged when the boss position changes (assert `boss.x`/`boss.y` separately from the bar's drawn position).
- `getHpFraction()` decreases monotonically with each hit from 1.0 toward 0.
- The four phase-segment dividers and the proportional fill are retained.
- All `Boss.test.ts` / `GymBoss.test.ts` assertions updated for 200 HP pass.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC1) **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- (parent AC4) **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
data.title: Retune boss HP to 200 and screen-fix the health bar

# Increase per-phase boss minion counts

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the Central AI boss reinforced by more minions so the fight feels dangerous; as a developer I want the counts defined once in the shared minion planner.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC2.

## Existing state

- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` `BOSS_MINION_WAVES`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `minionCountForPhase(phase)` derives counts from `wavePlannedSpawnCount(wave.groups)`.

## Desired change

Retune to P1 = **12 scouts (6 per side)**, P2 = **12 divers (6 per side)**, P3 = **0**, P4 = **15 swarm**. Keep formations, keys, shootEnabled flags and phase-3 emptiness unchanged.

## Key Files

- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — group counts/positions.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts` — per-phase count assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym minion-count expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `minionCountForPhase(1) === 12`, `=== 12` for phase 2, `=== 0` for phase 3, `=== 15` for phase 4.
- `planMinionSpawns(phase).length` matches `minionCountForPhase(phase)` for every phase.
- Phase 1 and phase 2 are split into two groups of 6; phase 4 is a single group of 15.
- Existing shootEnabled semantics per phase are unchanged.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC2) **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
data.title: Increase per-phase boss minion counts

# Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the boss to move in a figure-of-8 so the encounter is dynamic and I have to track my shots; as a developer I want the motion implemented once so `PlayScene` and every boss gym stay in parity.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC3.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss(dt)` calls `boss.update(this.time.now, dt*1000, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT)` for **both** the game and `GymBoss` — the correct shared per-frame home for motion.
- `GymFormationScene` calls `entity.applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, ...)` on its boss each tick.

## Desired change

1. In the shared boss core, trace a Gerono lemniscate (figure-8) about the boss's spawn **anchor**:
   `theta = 2*PI * elapsedMs / BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS`, `x = anchorX + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X * sin(theta)`,
   `y = anchorY + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y * sin(2*theta)`.
   Export `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X = 120`, `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y = 60`, `BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS = 8000`.
2. Accumulate motion time in `Boss.update(...)` (from `delta`) and set the boss position there, so both scenes get identical motion via `CombatScene._advanceBoss`.
3. Change `applyFormationPosition()` to set the **anchor** (not teleport the container), so the gym's per-frame call cannot fight the figure-8.
4. Clamp the traced position to the playfield bounds so the boss never leaves the screen.
5. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live `x`/`y`; the health bar does not move (delivered by the sibling health-bar task).

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — motion constants, state, `update()`, `applyFormationPosition()`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — confirm `_advanceBoss` drives motion for both scenes.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — traced-position and bounded-amplitude tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym motion parity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a deterministic `delta`, the boss position follows the lemniscate about its anchor with peak amplitudes ≈120 px horizontal and ≈60 px vertical and a full cycle of ≈8 s.
- The boss x/y stay within the playfield bounds across a full cycle.
- Calling `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, ...)` sets the anchor without overriding the live figure-8 position.
- The boss's live position is used for hit detection; the health bar's screen position is unchanged while the boss moves.
- Motion is implemented once in shared core (attributable to the sibling health-bar task that keeps the bar static).

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC3) **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
data.title: Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core

# Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want an obvious impact flash at the point where my shot hits the boss — every single hit — so I can see and hear that my fire is connecting.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the VFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` provides `spawnBulletImpact(scene, x, y, options)` (used by `CombatScene` for non-lethal multi-hit enemy feedback on the Harvester) with `radius`/`duration`/`registry` options.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` `takeDamage()` is the single shared point both `PlayScene._damageBoss()` and `GymBoss.damageBoss()` funnel through; it currently only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit and gives no per-hit feedback.
- `PlayScene.onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` / `onAoeHitsBoss` know the hit point (`pb.x`/`pb.y`); `GymBoss.damageBoss()` damages at the boss centre.

## Desired change

1. Extend `spawnBulletImpact` with an optional `color` option (default unchanged) so boss hits can use a hot impact colour.
2. Change `Boss.takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)` to play `playBossHitSound()` and spawn `spawnBulletImpact` at `(hitX ?? this.x, hitY ?? this.y)` on **every** landed hit. Retain the existing phase-transition cue on a depleting hit.
3. Track per-hit VFX in a small registry (`_hitEffects`) for test observability, removed on completion and torn down in `destroy()`.
4. Thread the hit point through `PlayScene._damageBoss(hitX?, hitY?)` from `onPlayerBulletHitsBoss`/`onAoeHitsBoss`; the gym calls `takeDamage()` at the boss centre.
5. Keep the feedback in the shared `Boss.takeDamage()` path so the game and gym cannot diverge.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — `takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)`, hit VFX/SFX, registry, teardown.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — optional `color` option.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — thread hit point through `_damageBoss`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — gym uses the shared path.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/vfx/bulletImpact.test.ts` — feedback tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every boss hit registers exactly one impact VFX at the supplied hit point (or the boss centre when none) and plays `playBossHitSound`.
- A depleting hit still plays the existing phase-transition cue in addition to the per-hit cue/VFX.
- Both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` receive the same feedback because it lives in shared `Boss.takeDamage()`.
- The VFX registry is emptied on completion and on `destroy()` (no leak / no orphan Graphics).
- Tests assert an impact effect is registered per hit and at the expected coordinates.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC5) **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
data.title: Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

# Verify gym-game parity and full test suite

## Goal / user story

As a developer, I want proof that the new boss behaviour is identical in the game and the boss gym, and that the whole suite is green, before the epic is reviewed.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC6 and AC8.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` is the repo-wide duplicate-body guard for shared gameplay behaviour.
- A gym-parity docs assertion also guards the parity convention (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1).

## Desired change

1. Add/extend parity assertions so the health bar screen position, figure-of-8 traced position, per-phase minion counts and per-hit feedback are identical (or driven by the same shared code) in `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`.
2. Confirm the duplicate-body guard and any parity docs assertion still pass with the new behaviour.
3. Run the full project test suite and fix any failures in-scope of this epic.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/*parity*` / docs parity test if present

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard passes; no divergent copy of boss movement or feedback exists in a gym.
- A test asserts the boss health bar's screen position is independent of the boss position in both the game and the gym.
- A test asserts the figure-8 position is produced by the shared core and matches between game and gym for the same `delta`.
- The full project test suite passes with no failures.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC6) **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
- (parent AC8) **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
data.title: Verify gym-game parity and full test suite

# Update boss encounter documentation

## Goal / user story

As a maintainer, I want the design and audio documentation to describe the new 200-hit, mobile, screen-fixed-health-bar boss with per-hit feedback, so docs match the shipped behaviour.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC7.

## Existing state

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.3 documents the 400-hit (100/phase) model and the static boss.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 documents the gym↔game parity convention.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` maps cues to ToneForge recipes.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` header comment describes the 4×100 health model.

## Desired change

Update all of the above to reflect: 200 total hits (4 × 50), the new per-phase minion counts (12/12/0/15), figure-8 movement (≈120 px / ≈60 px / ≈8 s, bounded), the screen-fixed top-centre health bar, and the dedicated boss-hit SFX + impact VFX. Add the new cue to the audio mapping. Use UK English. Keep the parity note accurate.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` (header/doc comments)

## Acceptance Criteria

- GDD §4.3 states 200 total hits (4 phases × 50), the minion counts, figure-8 movement parameters, the screen-fixed health bar and per-hit SFX/VFX.
- The audio cue mapping documents the new `playBossHitSound` → `aihell-boss-hit` entry.
- The parity documentation remains accurate (no divergent-copy claim) and any docs assertion test passes.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` comments no longer reference the old 100/400 model.
- All edits use UK English.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC7) **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
data.title: Update boss encounter documentation
